json.title: What kind of inhibitor is oxamate?
json.summary: Measure lactate dehydrogenase's initial rates across a range of pyruvate concentrations with and without oxamate, fit Km and Vmax to each set, and decide from how they change what kind of inhibitor oxamate is.
json.briefing: A competitive inhibitor competes with the substrate for the active site: enough substrate outcompetes it, so Vmax is unchanged but the apparent Km rises. A non-competitive inhibitor lowers Vmax and leaves Km alone; an uncompetitive one lowers both in proportion. Run both plates in the same way, so the only difference is the inhibitor.

json.title: Purifying a His-tagged protein on nickel
json.summary: Load a cleared E. coli lysate containing His-tagged GFP onto a nickel column, collect the flow-through, wash with 20 mM imidazole and elute with 250 mM imidazole. Follow the GFP by its absorbance at 488 nm to work out the yield, and check the purity of each fraction by SDS-PAGE.
json.briefing: Six histidines at the end of the protein hold it to the nickel; imidazole, which looks like histidine's side chain, competes it off. A little imidazole in the wash frees host proteins that stick weakly, without releasing the tagged one. GFP is green (A488), so you can follow it by eye and by absorbance; SDS-PAGE shows what else is in each fraction.
